Finally, it is more difficult to obtain high-quality images in some individuals than in others and in some muscles than in others. The reasons for these discrepancies are not always apparent, but lean individuals tend to be easier to scan than those carrying higher levels of body fat in the region of interest. In regard to scanning differences between muscles, some research indicates the posterior thigh is more difficult to visualize than the anterior thigh, potentially because of the geometry of the femur (2).
